questions.q: In SOQL, why does COUNT(Email) return a smaller number than COUNT(Id) when some leads have no email?
options: COUNT(field) counts only records where that field is not null
Both always return the same number
questions.explain: COUNT(fieldName) skips null values, so the gap between COUNT(Id) and COUNT(Email) is the number of blank emails.

questions.q: 214 duplicate email groups contain 468 leads in total. How many surplus records are there?
questions.explain: Each group keeps one record, so surplus equals 468 minus 214, which is 254.

questions.q: What should you do before fixing anything in a dirty dataset?
options: Delete every record with a blank field
Fill blanks with your best guess
Profile it with queries to measure nulls, duplicates, and inconsistent values
questions.explain: Profiling tells you what is wrong and how much, so you can decide what affects the dashboard and what to leave documented.

questions.q: Which step belongs in a safe Data Loader bulk-fix loop?
options: Update production first, then export a backup
Remove the Id column so rows cannot be matched
Test on a small sample, ideally in a sandbox, and review the success and error files
Skip verification because Data Loader is always correct
questions.explain: Export with Id and a backup, correct a copy, test small, update, then review error files and re-run profiling.

questions.q: After removing 254 duplicates, 3,600 leads become 3,346. With 540 conversions unaffected, what is the new conversion rate, roughly?
questions.explain: 540 divided by 3,346 is about 0.161, so the rate rises from 15.0 to about 16.1 percent.
